quartiers:Girona.name: Girona
quartiers:Girona.text: The inland capital and gastronomic pole: a medieval Old Town (Barri Vell) above the ochre Cases de l'Onyar restored in 1983–84, one of Europe's best-preserved Jewish quarters (El Call), and the orbit of the Roca brothers — El Celler de Can Roca (three stars since 2009), Restaurant Massana, the Mercat del Lleó, and Jordi Roca's Rocambolesc gelateria.

quartiers:Cadaqués & Portlligat.name: Cadaqués & Portlligat
quartiers:Cadaqués & Portlligat.text: A whitewashed fishing village at the tip of Cap de Creus, a cobbled maze that fixed itself in Dalí's imagination; Portlligat next door holds the house-museum, the fisherman's hut he bought in 1930 and worked in for fifty years. Compartir Cadaqués, from the elBulli trio, is the town's best table.

quartiers:Calella de Palafrugell & Llafr.name: Calella de Palafrugell & Llafranc
quartiers:Calella de Palafrugell & Llafr.text: Twin coves linked by the cliff-hugging camí de ronda, an arcaded fishermen's quarter (Les Voltes at Port Bo), the spiritual home of the garoinada. Casamar sits on the Llafranc headland, its door opening straight onto the path's steps.

quartiers:Palamós.name: Palamós
quartiers:Palamós.text: A working fishing port and home of the cult red prawn; the late-afternoon auction is the region's commercial heart. La Gamba on Plaça de Sant Pere, the Espai del Peix at the llotja, the Museu de la Pesca on the quay.

quartiers:L'Escala & Empúries.name: L'Escala & Empúries
quartiers:L'Escala & Empúries.text: The salt-and-anchovy town beside the only site in Iberia with both a Greek and a Roman city. The ruins of Empúries, the working salting houses, the Anchovy and Salt Museum, and Anxoves Solés on the Plaça de la Sardana.

quartiers:Roses.name: Roses
quartiers:Roses.text: The bay town carrying the elBulli legacy: the Cala Montjoi site reopened as the elBulli1846 museum on 15 June 2023, and Rafa's — a five-table counter beloved by Ferran Adrià — serves grilled and raw seafood with nothing else.

quartiers:Pals & Peratallada.name: Pals & Peratallada
quartiers:Pals & Peratallada.text: Two of the best-preserved medieval stone villages in Spain, ringed by the paddies of arròs de Pals (cultivated since 1452). Can Bonay sits under the arcades of the Plaça de les Voltes in Peratallada — pedra tallada, "carved stone."

quartiers:Out of town — Olot, La Garrotx.name: Out of town — Olot, La Garrotxa & Besalú
quartiers:Out of town — Olot, La Garrotx.text: The volcanic hinterland: Olot, capital of a natural park with forty-odd volcanic cones, and Besalú, a near-perfect medieval town with a fortified twelfth-century Pont Vell and a Jewish mikveh discovered in 1964 — the first found in Spain.

bougie:Castell de Perelada.name: Castell de Perelada
bougie:Castell de Perelada.hook: The DO's historic castle-estate, with a casino, gardens and the largest cellars in the appellation.
chips: Estate tour + tasting; the prestige reds and the cava
Book ahead, especially in festival season
Daytime tours; festival nights in summer
bougie:Castell de Perelada.text: The most important and largest winery of DO Empordà occupies a restored medieval castle at Peralada, with a full range from cava to prestige reds, a library, a casino and formal gardens. Estate tours and tastings turn the wine into an afternoon; the summer Festival Castell de Peralada brings opera and dance to the grounds.

bougie:El Celler de Can Roca — the cella.name: El Celler de Can Roca — the cellar
bougie:El Celler de Can Roca — the cella.hook: Josep Roca's cellar pairing is its own form of luxury, beyond the food.
chips: The full cellar pairing alongside the Festival menu
bougie:El Celler de Can Roca — the cella.text: Beyond the three-star kitchen, the prestige room here is the cellar — Josep "Pitu" Roca's wine programme, organised around five aromatic "worlds," is among the most ambitious sommellerie on the planet. The pairing is the reason serious drinkers cross continents for this table.

dish:Gamba de Palamós.name: Gamba de Palamós
dish:Gamba de Palamós.hook: The deep-water red prawn, sweeter than any other in the Mediterranean.
dish:Gamba de Palamós.text: Aristeus antennatus, trawled at 400 m and deeper off the canyon between Cap de Begur and the Ridaura, graded into three sizes and sold at the afternoon Dutch auction. Seared briefly with salt; the head, full of coral, is the prized part, sucked or grilled. Protected by the "Gamba de Palamós" quality mark. Eat it at La Gamba in Palamós or at Rafa's in Roses.

dish:Garoines (sea urchins).name: Garoines (sea urchins)
dish:Garoines (sea urchins).hook: Paracentrotus lividus, spooned raw from the half-shell in deep winter.
dish:Garoines (sea urchins).text: Hand-gathered by divers and at their peak from January to March, when the roe fills to a quarter of the animal's body weight. Eaten raw, half-opened, all iodine, with toasted bread and sometimes lemon, or worked into scrambled eggs and rice. The garoinada campaign across Palafrugell's three coves runs 16 Jan–29 Mar 2026.

dish:Anxoves de l'Escala.name: Anxoves de l'Escala
dish:Anxoves de l'Escala.hook: Salt-cured anchovies, a craft the town has practised since the 1700s.
dish:Anxoves de l'Escala.text: Engraulis encrasicolus layered head-to-tail in barrels with coarse salt, sealed under a salt cap, pressed and cured six to eighteen months, then hand-cleaned, deboned and laid one by one into tins of olive oil — historically the work of the anxoveres, passed mother to daughter. Buy them at Anxoves Solés .

dish:Suquet de peix.name: Suquet de peix
dish:Suquet de peix.hook: The fishermen's stew, born on the boats from unsold fish.
dish:Suquet de peix.text: Monkfish, escórpora (scorpionfish) and hake with potato, allioli and a mortar picada — garlic, parsley, nuts, fried bread, paprika, often a saffron-tomato sofregit. Its coastal cousin, suquet d'anxova, is strongest at Tossa de Mar and L'Escala. Definitive at Cal Tet .

dish:Arròs de Pals.name: Arròs de Pals
dish:Arròs de Pals.hook: Rice grown on the Baix Ter plain since 1452.
dish:Arròs de Pals.text: Bahia and Bomba traditionally, with newer Carnaroli and Nembo, grown around Pals inside the Montgrí–Medes–Baix Ter park. The long, mild Empordà autumn gives grains that hold their shape when cooked; they carry the local seafood arrossos. On the menus at Els Tinars and the coastal marisqueries.

dish:Recuit de drap.name: Recuit de drap
dish:Recuit de drap.hook: Fresh Empordà curd drained in its cloth, eaten with honey.
dish:Recuit de drap.text: Goat and/or sheep curd named for the drap (cloth) it drains and wraps in, its creaminess coming from a very long curdling of seventeen to twenty-four hours. Eaten with honey or sugar as dessert. Named producers include Mas Marcè/"Nuri" at Ullastret, Casa Martell in the Baix Empordà, and Làctics Pauet at Pau.

dish:Botifarra.name: Botifarra
dish:Botifarra.hook: Catalan fresh pork sausage, from blanca to the sweet dolça.
dish:Botifarra.text: Botifarra blanca and negra (raw or cooked), the cooked botifarra de perol of the Girona–Maresme, and the festive botifarra dolça — a dessert sausage sweetened with sugar and lemon, an Empordà curiosity. Served amb seques, with white beans. Find the embotits at the Mercat del Lleó .

drink:Garnatxa (Lledoner) — the three co.name: Garnatxa (Lledoner) — the three colours
drink:Garnatxa (Lledoner) — the three co.hook: White, grey and black Grenache, the spine of DO Empordà.
drink:Garnatxa (Lledoner) — the three co.text: Garnatxa, known locally as Lledoner, in its blanca, gris and negra forms, grown on low staked bush vines the tramuntana keeps dry and free of mildew. Old vines (vinyes velles) of fifty to a hundred and twenty years give low yields and concentration. Espelt at Vilajuïga and Vinyes dels Aspres at Cantallops are reference growers.

drink:Carinyena (Samsó).name: Carinyena (Samsó)
drink:Carinyena (Samsó).hook: Carignan, reintroduced from France by the Roig family in the 1890s.
drink:Carinyena (Samsó).text: Called Samsó locally, Carinyena is the other native red, often co-planted with Garnatxa in old field blends. The Roig family brought grafts back from France in the 1890s after phylloxera. It gives structure, acid and dark fruit to the Empordà reds.

drink:Garnatxa de l'Empordà (sweet).name: Garnatxa de l'Empordà (sweet)
drink:Garnatxa de l'Empordà (sweet).hook: The signature sweet wine — sun-dried, oxidative, fortified Grenache.
drink:Garnatxa de l'Empordà (sweet).text: A vi dolç natural made by sun-drying and oxidising Garnatxa, the lineage running from the Greeks at Empúries through the monks of Sant Pere de Rodes to today. Distinct from the dry reds, it is the dessert wine of the coast — try Mas Estela's Moscatell Estela and Estela Dolç Solera alongside it.

drink:Lledoner Roig (grey Grenache).name: Lledoner Roig (grey Grenache)
drink:Lledoner Roig (grey Grenache).hook: A Costa Brava rarity — almost all of Catalonia's plantings are here.
drink:Lledoner Roig (grey Grenache).text: Of roughly sixty-one hectares of Lledoner Roig in all Catalonia, about sixty sit in the Empordà. Pink-grey-skinned, it gives textured, faintly oxidative whites with weight and salinity — one of the most distinctive things the DO grows.

drink:Mas Estela — biodynamic.name: Mas Estela — biodynamic
drink:Mas Estela — biodynamic.hook: Sixteen hectares at Selva de Mar, biodynamic since 1999.
drink:Mas Estela — biodynamic.text: Organic from 1989 and biodynamic since 1999, hand-harvested estate fruit farmed to lunar and planetary cycles with no synthetic inputs — Grenache (noir and gris), Muscat, Syrah and Samsó. The cult names are Vinya Selva de Mar (red and white) and Quindals. The Cap de Creus terroir in a glass.

drink:Martín Faixó — Cadaqués.name: Martín Faixó — Cadaqués
drink:Martín Faixó — Cadaqués.hook: A family winery at 300 m on the Cadaqués pass, inside the Cap de Creus park.
drink:Martín Faixó — Cadaqués.text: About eleven hectares at three hundred metres on the Cadaqués pass, "surrounded by the sea" inside the natural park — Picapoll, Muscat and Grenache under the Cadaqués brand. The dramatic coastal-mountain setting, schist underfoot and tramuntana overhead, is the signature.

drink:La Vinyeta — natural.name: La Vinyeta — natural
drink:La Vinyeta — natural.hook: A young mixed farm at Mollet de Peralada reviving the old masia model.
drink:La Vinyeta — natural.text: A small, sustainability-minded estate combining vines, olives and cattle, making natural wines without added sulphites alongside its own olive oil and honey — the new-generation Empordà spirit. Drink it by the glass at La Tabarra in Girona.

music:Festival Castell de Peralada.name: Festival Castell de Peralada
music:Festival Castell de Peralada.hook: Summer opera and dance in the gardens of the Perelada castle.
music:Festival Castell de Peralada.text: The region's flagship classical festival stages opera, recitals and ballet in the open-air gardens and the castle's church and cloister through July and August — the cultural high point of the Empordà summer.

music:Cap Roig Festival.name: Cap Roig Festival
music:Cap Roig Festival.hook: Big-name concerts in the cliff-top botanical gardens above Calella.
music:Cap Roig Festival.text: Held in the terraced botanical gardens of Cap Roig between Calella de Palafrugell and Palamós, this summer festival brings international pop, jazz and classical acts to a stage hanging over the sea.

music:Cantada d'Havaneres, Calella de Pa.name: Cantada d'Havaneres, Calella de Palafrugell
music:Cantada d'Havaneres, Calella de Pa.hook: The habanera sea-shanty gathering, first Saturday of July.
music:Cantada d'Havaneres, Calella de Pa.text: On the beach at Port Bo, the famous havaneres singalong — Cuban-rooted sailors' songs sung over cremat (flamed rum) — is the most local musical tradition on the coast, drawing thousands to Calella's cove.

culture:Teatre-Museu Dalí, Figueres.name: Teatre-Museu Dalí, Figueres
culture:Teatre-Museu Dalí, Figueres.hook: Dalí's own surrealist monument, built on a ruined theatre, his final resting place.
chips: Timed ticket; the Mae West room, the Rainy Taxi
culture:Teatre-Museu Dalí, Figueres.text: Salvador Dalí was born in Figueres on 11 May 1904, and built his theatre-museum on the bombed shell of the town's old theatre — a total Surrealist environment crowned with eggs and golden bread loaves. He is buried in its crypt. The anchor of the Dalí Triangle.

culture:Salvador Dalí House-Museum, Port.name: Salvador Dalí House-Museum, Portlligat
culture:Salvador Dalí House-Museum, Port.hook: The fisherman's hut Dalí bought in 1930 and lived in for fifty years.
chips: Book the timed small-group visit well ahead
culture:Salvador Dalí House-Museum, Port.text: On the cove next to Cadaqués, Dalí expanded a single barraca into a labyrinthine home by buying adjacent huts, living and working here from 1930 to 1982 with Gala. The eroded schist of Cap de Creus outside is the literal landscape behind his melting forms. Entry is by small timed groups only.

culture:Ruïnes d'Empúries.name: Ruïnes d'Empúries
culture:Ruïnes d'Empúries.hook: The Greek Emporion and the Roman city beside it, on the L'Escala shore.
chips: Combined ticket with the archaeology museum
culture:Ruïnes d'Empúries.text: Founded around 575 BCE by Greeks from Massalia as Emporion, "the market," and occupied by Rome from 218 BCE as the bridgehead for the conquest of Hispania. The Palaiapolis at Sant Martí, the Neapolis on the mainland, and the Roman city above — walk it with the sea on one side.

culture:Cap de Creus Natural Park.name: Cap de Creus Natural Park
culture:Cap de Creus Natural Park.hook: The easternmost point of Iberia, where the Pyrenees plunge into the sea.
chips: Drive or walk to the Cap de Creus lighthouse
Open access; visitor centre at Palau de Tudela
culture:Cap de Creus Natural Park.text: About 14,000 hectares of Precambrian schist 580–540 million years old, folded by the Variscan orogeny into the contorted shear zones of the Paratge de Tudela — the wind- and sea-sculpted rock that fed Dalí's imagery. A geological textbook with a lighthouse at the tip.

culture:Sant Pere de Rodes.name: Sant Pere de Rodes
culture:Sant Pere de Rodes.hook: The Benedictine monastery on the Verdera slope that kept the vines alive.
chips: Combine with a hike up the Verdera massif
culture:Sant Pere de Rodes.text: A great Romanesque monastery on the mountainside above the Gulf of Roses, a key medieval landholder that carried Empordà viticulture through the Middle Ages. The view from its terrace runs the length of the coast to Cap de Creus.

culture:Santa Maria de Castelló d'Empúri.name: Santa Maria de Castelló d'Empúries
culture:Santa Maria de Castelló d'Empúri.hook: The "Cathedral of l'Empordà" — a Gothic church in a former county capital.
chips: The carved alabaster retable and the tower
culture:Santa Maria de Castelló d'Empúri.text: Rebuilt in Gothic style in the late thirteenth century and so grand for a small town that locals call it the Cathedral of l'Empordà, it marks Castelló d'Empúries' centuries as seat of the Counts of Empúries. Often overlooked by visitors heading straight for the coast.

culture:elBulli1846, Cala Montjoi (Roses.name: elBulli1846, Cala Montjoi (Roses)
culture:elBulli1846, Cala Montjoi (Roses.hook: Ferran Adrià's legendary restaurant, reopened as a museum in 2023.
chips: Book the timed visit; the access road is rough
Seasonal (roughly half the year); reserve online
culture:elBulli1846, Cala Montjoi (Roses.text: The cove above Roses where elBulli was five times the world's best restaurant is now a museum of creativity — 69 multimedia installations across some 4,000 m², named for the 1,846 dishes the team created. It runs as a six-month museum and becomes the elBulliDNA research lab off-season.

culture:Besalú.name: Besalú
culture:Besalú.hook: A near-perfect medieval town with the first Jewish mikveh found in Spain.
chips: The Pont Vell, the mikveh, then on to Olot
Free town; mikveh guided visit small fee
culture:Besalú.text: Inland on the way to La Garrotxa, Besalú is crossed by a fortified eleventh-to-twelfth-century bridge of seven arches and holds a twelfth-century Jewish ritual bath, the mikveh discovered in 1964 — the first found in Spain. The volcanic Garrotxa park and the painters' town of Olot lie just beyond.

work:La Fábrica, Girona.name: La Fábrica, Girona
work:La Fábrica, Girona.hook: Specialty coffee and a long table, the cyclists' clubhouse.
work:La Fábrica, Girona.text: Girona's pioneering third-wave café in the Barri Vell — single-origin filters, a wifi-friendly room, and the pro-cycling community at the next table. The most natural place in the Old Town to sit with a laptop over a flat white.

work:Plaça de la Independència terraces,.name: Plaça de la Independència terraces, Girona
work:Plaça de la Independència terraces,.hook: Arcaded neoclassical square on the Onyar's west bank.
work:Plaça de la Independència terraces,.text: The porticoed square in the Mercadal is lined with cafés under the arcades — sit out of the sun with a coffee and the river a block away, between market runs and museum visits.

work:Jardins de Cap Roig, Calella de Pal.name: Jardins de Cap Roig, Calella de Palafrugell
work:Jardins de Cap Roig, Calella de Pal.hook: Cliff-top botanical gardens hanging over the sea.
work:Jardins de Cap Roig, Calella de Pal.text: Terraced gardens of Mediterranean plants on the headland between Calella and Palamós — benches with the sea below, a quiet place to read away from the coves' crowds. A small entry fee.

work:Riva of Cadaqués at dusk.name: Riva of Cadaqués at dusk
work:Riva of Cadaqués at dusk.hook: The whitewashed seafront under the church.
work:Riva of Cadaqués at dusk.text: The waterfront promenade of Cadaqués, boats drawn up on the pebbles and the white church above, is where the village slows at the end of the day — a café table, a notebook, the light Dalí chased.

events:La Garoinada.name: La Garoinada
events:La Garoinada.hook: 16 Jan – 29 Mar 2026, Palafrugell + Calella, Llafranc, Tamariu
events:La Garoinada.text: The sea-urchin campaign running since 1992 across Palafrugell and its three coves, a dozen-plus restaurants serving garoina menus at the winter peak. Tasting menus around €65. Verify the exact 2026 dates with each restaurant.

events:Calçotada season.name: Calçotada season
events:Calçotada season.text: Charred calçots (long spring onions) peeled by hand and dipped in romesco, eaten outdoors with red wine and botifarra — the great Catalan winter feast, peaking in the first months of the year.

events:Cantada d'Havaneres, Calella de P.name: Cantada d'Havaneres, Calella de Palafrugell
events:Cantada d'Havaneres, Calella de P.hook: First Saturday of July, Port Bo beach
events:Cantada d'Havaneres, Calella de P.text: The famous habanera singalong on Calella's cove — Cuban-rooted sailors' songs over flamed cremat rum, drawing thousands to the beach in early July. Verify the year's date.

events:Festival Castell de Peralada.name: Festival Castell de Peralada
events:Festival Castell de Peralada.text: Opera, recitals and ballet in the open-air gardens and church of the Perelada castle estate through high summer — the region's flagship classical festival.

events:Cap Roig Festival.name: Cap Roig Festival
events:Cap Roig Festival.text: International pop, jazz and classical concerts in the cliff-top botanical gardens between Calella de Palafrugell and Palamós, with the sea below the stage.

events:Fira d'Indians, Begur.name: Fira d'Indians, Begur
events:Fira d'Indians, Begur.text: Begur's colonial-revival fair celebrating its nineteenth-century Indiano mansions, built by returnees from Cuba — Caribbean music, rum and costume through the hilltop streets. Verify the year's dates.

walks:Camí de ronda: Calella → Llafranc.name: Camí de ronda: Calella → Llafranc
walks:Camí de ronda: Calella → Llafranc.hook: Dawn at Port Bo · 5.5 km · ~1.5–2 hrs · 164 m climb
walks:Camí de ronda: Calella → Llafranc.text: The signature coastal walk: from the Les Voltes arches at Calella, the cliff-cut camí de ronda through pine, El Canadell, rock tunnels and the door of Casamar to Llafranc's bay and the Sant Sebastià lighthouse.

walks:Cadaqués lanes at dawn.name: Cadaqués lanes at dawn
walks:Cadaqués lanes at dawn.hook: First light · the cobbled maze · ~45 min
walks:Cadaqués lanes at dawn.text: The whitewashed labyrinth of Cadaqués before the day-trippers — church bell, fishing boats in Portlligat bay, the alternative dawn walk to the Palafrugell coves.

walks:Cap de Creus to the lighthouse.name: Cap de Creus to the lighthouse
walks:Cap de Creus to the lighthouse.hook: Paratge de Tudela · sculpted schist · 1–2 hrs
walks:Cap de Creus to the lighthouse.text: From the Palau de Tudela across the surreal wind- and sea-carved rock formations of the Paratge de Tudela to the lighthouse at the easternmost point of Iberia — the Dalí landscape in three dimensions.

walks:Empúries shore path.name: Empúries shore path
walks:Empúries shore path.hook: Sant Martí d'Empúries → L'Escala · seafront · ~30 min
walks:Empúries shore path.text: Along the ancient harbour from the medieval hamlet of Sant Martí d'Empúries past the Greek and Roman ruins to L'Escala, the Mediterranean on one side and two thousand five hundred years of trade on the other.

walks:Pals to the rice paddies.name: Pals to the rice paddies
walks:Pals to the rice paddies.hook: Gothic hilltop core · the Baix Ter plain · flat
walks:Pals to the rice paddies.text: From the stone lanes of medieval Pals out across the rice fields of the Baix Ter — the paddies worked since 1452, flat and green under the Montgrí massif.

secret-gems:The Les Voltes arches at Por.name: The Les Voltes arches at Port Bo, at dawn
secret-gems:The Les Voltes arches at Por.text: Boats drawn up on the sand, the smell of brine, pine and tar, under the whitewashed arches — before the camí de ronda wakes for the day.

secret-gems:The sculpted schist of the P.name: The sculpted schist of the Paratge de Tudela
secret-gems:The sculpted schist of the P.text: Rock folded and polished by wind and sea, one outcrop nicknamed "the Eagle" — the precise landscape behind Dalí's melting forms, free and almost always empty.

secret-gems:The terrace of Sant Pere de.name: The terrace of Sant Pere de Rodes
secret-gems:The terrace of Sant Pere de.text: From the monastery forecourt the coast unrolls to Cap de Creus; the wind, the Romanesque stone, and almost nobody out of season.

secret-gems:The Onyar footbridges, Giron.name: The Onyar footbridges, Girona
secret-gems:The Onyar footbridges, Giron.text: The ochre and terracotta houses restored in 1983–84 reflected in the river; from the bridge, the Jewish quarter rising behind — a quarter-hour of free contemplation.

secret-gems:The square of Sant Martí d'E.name: The square of Sant Martí d'Empúries
secret-gems:The square of Sant Martí d'E.text: The medieval hamlet where the Greek Palaiapolis stood, a shaded square at the sea's edge a few steps from the ruins — a coffee and two and a half thousand years of history.

secret-gems:The pebble cove of Sa Tuna.name: The pebble cove of Sa Tuna
secret-gems:The pebble cove of Sa Tuna.text: A handful of fishermen's houses and boats hauled up on the shingle below Begur — the Costa Brava before tourism, out of season.

ethnic-restaurants:North African and Lat.name: North African and Latin American shops, around the Mercat del Lleó
details: Plaça de Francesc Calvet i Rubalcaba, 17002 Girona
ethnic-restaurants:North African and Lat.text: A handful of shops around the market and the train station serve Girona's North African and Latin American communities — spices, harissa, tinned goods. For a wider range (East and South Asian), Barcelona, an hour away by train, remains the reference.

street-food:Pa amb tomàquet.name: Pa amb tomàquet
street-food:Pa amb tomàquet.text: The Catalan opening ritual: bread rubbed with ripe tomato, Empordà olive oil and salt — the base on which the salt anchovy and the ham are laid.

street-food:Coca de recapte / coca d'anx.name: Coca de recapte / coca d'anxoves
street-food:Coca de recapte / coca d'anx.text: A flat oven-baked flatbread topped with grilled vegetables (escalivada) or L'Escala anchovies — the Catalan pizza without cheese, sold at village bakeries.

street-food:Panet (gelato in brioche) at.name: Panet (gelato in brioche) at Rocambolesc
street-food:Panet (gelato in brioche) at.text: The street dessert of the Roca universe: artisan gelato slid into a warm brioche, by Jordi Roca — the most accessible of the three brothers.

gastronomy:Mercat del Lleó, Girona.name: Mercat del Lleó, Girona
gastronomy:Mercat del Lleó, Girona.text: Girona's historic 1944 covered market, around sixty stalls where the city's chefs shop. Seasonal bolets (wild mushrooms), local embotits, Empordà cheeses, and fish landed at Roses and Palamós. Arrive before it closes at half past one; closed Sunday.

gastronomy:Llotja de Palamós (fish aucti.name: Llotja de Palamós (fish auction)
gastronomy:Llotja de Palamós (fish aucti.text: The working fish auction on the Moll Pesquer, where the gamba de Palamós is graded and sold at a descending Dutch auction. Watch it through the window from the Espai del Peix, which also runs guided visits and show-cooking on the quay.

gastronomy:Espelt Viticultors.name: Espelt Viticultors
gastronomy:Espelt Viticultors.text: The largest of the named DO Empordà growers, around two hundred hectares, organic for over twenty years and focused on native varieties — now led by Anna Espelt, with a modern winery beside the family farmhouse and a second estate, Mas Marès, above Cala Montjoi.

gastronomy:Celler Mas Estela.name: Celler Mas Estela
gastronomy:Celler Mas Estela.hook: Selva de Mar (Cap de Creus) — biodynamic since 1999
gastronomy:Celler Mas Estela.text: Sixteen hectares of estate fruit farmed biodynamically since 1999 to lunar and planetary cycles — Grenache, Muscat, Syrah and Samsó, hand-harvested. The cult names are Vinya Selva de Mar and Quindals, plus the sweet Moscatell Estela.

gastronomy:Celler Martín Faixó.name: Celler Martín Faixó
gastronomy:Celler Martín Faixó.hook: Cadaqués — 300 m inside the Cap de Creus park
gastronomy:Celler Martín Faixó.text: A family winery of about eleven hectares on the Cadaqués pass at three hundred metres, surrounded by the sea inside the natural park — Picapoll, Muscat and Grenache under the Cadaqués brand.

gastronomy:Anxoves Solés.name: Anxoves Solés
gastronomy:Anxoves Solés.text: The heritage anchovy house of L'Escala, founded in 1888 by Francisco Solés Oliveras and run by five generations, salt-curing anchovies the traditional way and running a factory-museum in town.

gastronomy:Empordàlia (Oli de Pau).name: Empordàlia (Oli de Pau)
gastronomy:Empordàlia (Oli de Pau).hook: Pau — the DOP olive-oil and wine cooperative
gastronomy:Empordàlia (Oli de Pau).text: Formed in 1995 from the old Pau, Roses and Vilajuïga oil cooperatives, Empordàlia presses DOP Oli de l'Empordà from the native Argudell olive under the Oli de Pau and ADN Argudell brands — clean, fruity, balanced bitter-pungent oil — alongside its wines.

gastronomy:Anxoves Solés shop, L'Escala.name: Anxoves Solés shop, L'Escala
gastronomy:Anxoves Solés shop, L'Escala.hook: The definitive Empordà larder souvenir, on the Plaça de la Sardana.
gastronomy:Anxoves Solés shop, L'Escala.text: Salt-cured anchovy fillets in olive oil, whole salted anchovies and seitons (boquerones), bought at source from a five-generation house. The other historic producer, Anxoves de l'Escala, is nearby.

gastronomy:Rocambolesc, Girona.name: Rocambolesc, Girona
gastronomy:Rocambolesc, Girona.hook: Jordi Roca's gelateria — the Roca universe you can walk into.
gastronomy:Rocambolesc, Girona.text: The panet (gelato in brioche), the soft-serve with toppings from the Willy-Wonka cart, and seasonal Roca flavours on the Carrer de Santa Clara — the most accessible taste of the three-star brothers, no booking required.

avoid:Lloret de Mar beachfront strip.name: Lloret de Mar beachfront strip
avoid:Lloret de Mar beachfront strip.hook: Lloret de Mar — the front-line promenade — package-resort food and €28 photo-paella.
avoid:Lloret de Mar beachfront strip.text: Souvenir shops, generic clubs and tourist-menú paella joints. Step back into the old town or out to Fenals and Cala Boadella; better still, eat at the working ports of Palamós, L'Escala and Roses instead.

avoid:Front-line \"tourist menú\" paella.name: Front-line "tourist menú" paella
avoid:Front-line \"tourist menú\" paella.hook: Any resort promenade — the €25 paella-with-sangría photo board.
avoid:Front-line \"tourist menú\" paella.text: Reheated, saffron-coloured rice aimed at footfall, anywhere a board shows a photo of the dish. Real arròs is one street back, or at the rice and seafood houses inland.

avoid:High-August front-line dining.name: High-August front-line dining
avoid:High-August front-line dining.hook: The busy coves in peak August — crowds, queues, marked-up menus.
avoid:High-August front-line dining.text: This coast keeps its best season in winter and shoulder months. In high August the coves are full and prices climb; come for the garoinada, the spring, or the autumn instead.

avoid:Unverified phone bookings.name: Unverified phone bookings
avoid:Unverified phone bookings.hook: Phone numbers in this guide are intentionally blank.
avoid:Unverified phone bookings.text: No phone numbers are listed because none were independently verified. Book through each venue's website or Google Maps listing, and confirm the 2026 garoinada and festival dates directly.
